claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation selectively promotes formation of a Cr-rich oxide on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A pre-formed protective oxide layer can enhance elevated-temperature wear resistance.
The Cr-rich oxide tribofilm is self-healing.
The Cr-rich oxide tribofilm is load-bearing.
The Cr-rich oxide tribofilm is lubricious.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a fine-grained microstructure.
The baseline coating has no engineered or pre-formed oxide layer.
Optimization of pre-oxidation temperature, time, and oxygen partial pressure can selectively enrich the FeNiCrCoCu surface in Cr.
The pre-oxidation treatment produces a coherent Cr-rich oxide tribofilm that remains adherent during wear.
During high-temperature sliding, the pre-oxidized surface enables continuous regeneration of the Cr-rich oxide layer.
A protective oxide layer reduces wear by limiting direct metal-to-metal contact.
The oxide tribofilm bears the sliding load.
The pre-oxidized coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating at elevated temperature.
The pre-oxidized coating will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than the as-deposited coating.
The hypothesis is scoped to high-load sliding at approximately 500–700 °C.
The exact oxide phase composition, thickness, and durability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only if a continuous, adherent, self-healing Cr-rich film is successfully produced, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to observe such a film as falsification. Under the boundary, failure to form the film would instead fall outside the stated domain of applicability.
